newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Bardot fails to stop ex-husband's book.
newsitem.headline: France's Bardot fails to stop ex-husband's book.

text.p: A French court on Tuesday rejected a request by former film sex symbol Brigitte Bardot to make large cuts in a book her ex-husband Jacques Charrier wrote about their marriage.

Judge Renard Payen admitted the book intruded into Bardot's private life but it did not justify infringing Charrier's freedom of expression. Payen said Bardot herself had disclosed the facts cited by her ex-husband.
Bardot had asked that description of her intimate life with Charrier, love letters she once wrote to him and pictures of her be deleted from the book, "My Reply to BB".
The court also rejected her demand for 300,000 francs ($55,000) in damages and her request to halt the sale of the book, which was published 10 days ago, until the deletions were made.
Charrier, Bardot's husband from 1959 to 1963, called her a sexual "tease" in the book, written in response to her best-selling memoirs "Initiales BB".

The 62-year-old actress-turned-animal-rights-campaigner had described him as "a vulgar, dictatorial and uncontrolled macho, a gigolo, alcoholic and despicable" and their baby as "a tumour feeding off me".
Charrier and his son Nicolas, now 36, failed to have Bardot's memoirs stripped of 80 pages referring to them, but a court awarded them 250,000 francs ($43,000) in damages.
